item.title: LAB: Europe's borders through time, 1914 to 1947 (data for lessons) v0.3
item.snippet: Test layer for the time slider: every change to country borders in Europe from 1914 to 1947, with the dates each border was in force. Draft.
item.description:
Test layer. Every border in Europe that the source records between 1 January 1914 and 31 December 1947: 108 areas, each with its name at the time, its status, who controlled it if it was not independent, and dates.

For the time slider: use ShowFrom as the start field and ShowTo as the end field. They are the dates the border was in force, cut to 1914 to 1947. BorderFrom and BorderTo are the source's own dates, which can run earlier or later.

Limits: the source records recognised borders, not wartime occupation: Poland, Czechoslovakia, Austria and others stay on the map through the Second World War. The Free City of Danzig ends on 31 August 1938 in the source. The smallest states and some special territories are left out, and the Soviet Union is one area. Coastlines are simplified. Clipped at 60 degrees east, except the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union, which are shown whole.

Outlines: thinned to about a third of the source's points so the map draws faster; a line can sit up to about 3 kilometres from the source's in Europe and about 25 kilometres east of 60 degrees. The smallest islands are dropped.

Source: CShapes 2.0: Schvitz, Girardin, Ruegger, Weidmann, Cederman and Gleditsch (2022), Mapping the International System, 1886-2019, Journal of Conflict Resolution 66(1); ETH Zurich.

Data version 0.3 (26 November 2026): the Russian Empire and the Soviet Union shown whole, lab draft.
